## Summary of key points over the past 24 hours

• Over the past 24 hours, 85 new confirmed cases (29 new deaths) of Ebola Virus Disease (MVE) were recorded in the provinces of Ituri (68 cases), Nord-Kivu (10 cases) and Haut-Uélé (7 cases), reflecting the continuation of active transmission, mainly in Ituri.

• To date, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has accumulated 4 294 confirmed cases including 1 960 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 45,6 %.

Ituri remains the epicentre of the outbreak, accounting for 86,4 % of cumulative confirmed cases and 82,0% of new cases reported over the past 24 hours.

• 21 patients were declared recovered in Ituri after obtaining two negative MVE results and 15 intra-CTE deaths were recorded in Ituri and Nord Kivu.

• The outbreak affects 53 of the 140 health zones in the five concerned provinces.

Ituri accounts for 28 affected health zones out of 36, followed by Nord-Kivu (12/34), Haut-Uélé (6/13), Tshopo (6/23) and Sud-Kivu (1/34), confirming the geographical spread of the disease.

## 1. RESPONSE ACTIONS BY PILLAR

### 1.1. Coordination

#### 1.1.1. Main Actions

• Nord-Kivu: Joint WHO-DPS mission in the ZS (health zone) of Vuhovi, to evaluate the functionality of the zonal response coordination.

#### 1.1.2. Challenges

• Furthermore, several strategic actions essential to the decentralisation of coordination remain pending, notably the establishment and operationalisation of the sub-coordinations of Wamba, Pawa and Watsa.

This delay reduces coordination capacities at the operational level and requires an acceleration of the administrative, logistical and organisational arrangements needed to make these sub-coordinations fully functional.

### 1.2. Epidemiological surveillance

#### 1.2.1. Main Actions

1 282 alerts were recorded and verified in the five affected provinces for the day of 08 August 2026, of which 258 (20,1%) were validated as suspected cases and 258 (100%) were investigated and 124 suspects transferred to CT (transit centre)/CTE.

Contact tracing is at 84,6 % (14 505 seen out of 17 141 to follow up), corresponding to the threshold of 85 %, with weak performances in Haut-Uélé (76,1 %) and Nord-Kivu (80,2 %) ; Ituri reaches 87,7%.

#### 1.2.2. Challenges

Low reporting of alerts and listing and tracing of contacts around confirmed cases

### 1.3. Update on control point and point of entry (PoC/PoE) activities

#### 1.3.1. Main actions

Nine alerts were detected at PoE/PoC (7 in Ituri, 2 in Haut-Uélé): the five living alerts from Ituri were validated, isolated and referred to care facilities; the two lifeless bodies intercepted at Ariwara were not sampled, due to lack of an available SDB team, and none of those from Haut-Uélé was validated.

135 404 travellers were screened (117 337 in Ituri, 18 067 in Haut-Uélé), with a screening rate of 97,4 %.

/strategic PoC out of 18 (5,6 %) operated without interruption, compared to 100 %.

#### 1.3.2. Challenges

• Insufficient operationalisation of PoE/PoC: the functionality of PoE and PoC remains low in Haut-Uélé, with only 10 out of 38 (26,3 %) operational.

• Constraints affecting the functionality of PoE/PoC: performances remain affected by stockouts of supplies, PPE and water in Haut-Uélé, non-payment of providers, as well as non-compliance with the health protocol by certain authorities at the PoC of Mukulia (Nord-Kivu).

These constraints reduce the effectiveness of health screening, early detection and surveillance at borders and along main mobility axes.

### 1.4. Laboratory

#### 1.4.1. Main actions

• 400 samples were analysed, confirming 85 new cases of MVE (positivity: 21,3 %).

• Ituri recorded 68 positive results including 24 deaths, while Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uélé confirmed 10 (5 deaths) and 7 cases respectively.

#### 1.4.2. Challenges

High proportion of positive samples in Ituri (26,0 %) and incomplete reporting of laboratory results in Haut-Uélé and Tshopo (no data transmitted), limiting biological surveillance and real-time monitoring of MVE transmission.

### 1.5. Infection Prevention and Control (PCI (infection prevention and control)/EDS)

#### 1.5.1. Main actions

• In Ituri, 25 rings were opened (92 in total), 85 sites identified and 39 decontaminated (45 %) ; 66 SDB performed out of 82 death alerts (80,5 %) and 50 bodies sampled post-mortem, despite completeness limited to 10 ZS out of 29 (34 %).

• In Nord-Kivu, 76 health facilities supported and 229 providers briefed; 7 case-stay facilities decontaminated, 36 SDB performed and 37 bodies sampled and secured, for a completeness of 4 ZS out of 12.

• Tshopo did not transmit any PCI/EDS data.

#### 1.5.2. Challenges

Low implementation of PCI standards: very low reporting completeness in Ituri (34 %) and Nord-Kivu (4 ZS out of 12), partial decontamination of identified sites in Ituri (39 out of 85) and low scorecards in Nord-Kivu (30,3 % in Beni and 31,4 % in Kalunguta), demonstrating a continuous risk of healthcare-associated infections.

### 1.6. Continuity of care

#### 1.6.1. Main actions

• In Ituri, 29 ambulances were allocated to the response, 26 of which were available; 28 runs completed, 26 of which successfully, for 29 evacuated patients.

CTEs/CTs recorded 73 admissions and 82 discharges, including 21 recovered; occupancy reached 501 patients for 840 beds (60 %), with saturation of the CTEs of Rwampara, ISTM and Nizi and the CT of Bambu.

• In Nord-Kivu, 239 cumulative admissions in the CTEs/CTs, including 208 confirmed cases, for an intra-CTE mortality of 39 %; 66 admissions, no recovered today while 6 intra-CTE deaths were reported.

• In Haut-Uélé: lack of a standard CTE persists in the 6 affected health zones

#### 1.6.2. Challenges

Insufficient availability of referral means (3 broken-down ambulances in Ituri, absence of an ambulance in 7 ZS of Nord-Kivu) and saturation of several CTEs/CTs, limiting rapid access to care and isolation of suspects.

### 1.7. Risk communication and community engagement

#### 1.7.1. Main actions

• In Ituri, mass awareness-raising of 100 traders at the Sukisa 2 market and support to 20 community relays during door-to-door visits in the health zone of Rwampara; 4 213 people reached during home visits

• In Nord-Kivu, 17 community leaders were briefed and a guided visit of the CTE of Kitatumba organised; 16 rumours were clarified, 5 community incidents resolved and 129 household heads reached around 25 cases.

• In Haut-Uélé, 2 332 people reached during visits to 749 households in Isiro, Wamba and Pawa, 30 motorcycle-taxi drivers sensitized in Wamba and 66 IEC tools distributed (cumulative: 351).

#### 1.7.2. Challenges

Persistence of community challenges: demotivation of actors linked to non-payment for more than two months in Nord-Kivu, denial of MVE and opposition to an SDB in Isiro, repeated expectations regarding vaccine availability, likely to affect community adherence to response interventions

### 1.8. Logistics

#### 1.8.1. Main actions

In Ituri: installed capacity reaches 840 beds (412 for confirmed cases, 428 for suspected cases); expansion of the CTEs of Bambu, Nizi and Logo is requested in view of saturation.

In Nord-Kivu: continuation of unpacking of the WHO donation of PCI kits, preparation of orders for the ZSs of Vuhovi and Musienene and delivery of infant milk to the ZS of Butembo; work in progress on tank bases at the PoCs of Karuruma and Komba and for the triage unit of HGR (general referral hospital) Vuhovi (ULB Coopération).

#### 1.8.2. Challenges

Persistence of logistical needs to support the expansion of the response, notably completion of CTE expansions, continuous supply of essential commodities and PPE, and availability of transport and evacuation means

### 1.9. Security

#### 1.9.1. Main actions

• In Nord-Kivu, 13 security escorts were provided to the SDB and PCI teams in Lubero and Katwa; intervention by the security team in Katwa, by warning shots, faced with an attempt by the population to retrieve the body of a confirmed case.

#### 1.9.2. Challenges

• Persistent insecurity, incidents involving political authorities and community resistance during safe and dignified burials, limiting access of response teams, continuity of interventions and coverage of activities in certain affected zones: attempt to retrieve the body of a confirmed case by the population in Katwa (Nord-Kivu) and 15 safe and dignified burials postponed to the next day in Ituri.

### 1.10. PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse)

#### 1.10.1. Main actions

Continuation of awareness-raising activities on the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) in different communities of the affected provinces.

#### 1.10.2. Challenges

Still insufficient coverage of awareness-raising activities and reinforcement of mechanisms for prevention, reporting and management of cases of sexual exploitation and abuse across all zones concerned by the response

## KEY MESSAGES

• Transmission of MVE remains active, with 85 new cases and 29 confirmed deaths recorded over the past 24 hours, bringing the national cumulative total to 4 294 confirmed cases and 1 960 deaths.

• Ituri remains the epicentre of the outbreak, concentrating 86,4 % of cumulative confirmed cases and 82,0% of new cases reported over the past 24 hours and a larger expansion (28 of the 36 health zones affected).

• Surveillance shows good performance over the past 24h, with 100% of alerts investigated and a follow-up rate of 84,6% corresponding to the threshold of 85,0%.

• Strengthening priority interventions (surveillance, patient care, PCI, logistics and community engagement) remains essential to rapidly interrupt chains of transmission.

## CHRONOLOGY OF KEY EVENTS

• From 24 April to 15 May 2026, the outbreak evolved from the detection of the first suspected cases to biological confirmation of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, leading to the official declaration of the 17th Ebola Virus Disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

• Between 17 and 18 May 2026, national authorities, with the support of partners, reinforced the response by declaring a public health emergency of national and then continental concern, accompanied by the mobilisation of coordination and support mechanisms.
